A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Talk2Event dataset and EventRefer framework. Their main text, equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A–E are readable and can be matched reliably despite pagination changes.

before.justification: v1 reports original grounding experiments across three input modalities, component and attribute ablations, expert-activation analyses, and additional quantitative and qualitative results in Appendix C.

after.justification: v2 retains the original benchmark experiments, ablations, and appendix analyses, including the reported outcomes in Tables 2–5 and 14–16.

M1.justification: Positive word matching, the mixture of event-attribute experts, co-located attribute supervision, and inference-time scoring remain unchanged in Section 4. No algorithmic component or procedure is added or revised.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same DSEC-derived Talk2Event coverage: seven traffic-object categories, 5,567 scenes, and 30,690 expressions. Frame-only, event-only, and event-frame fusion tasks and the appendix scenarios are retained.

E2.justification: Table 2 and Appendix Tables 14–16 retain identical comparator sets within each modality, including OWL-v2, EvRT-DETR, DAGr, and FlexEvent. The fusion-strategy comparators in Table 5 also remain unchanged.

E3.justification: The splits, preprocessing, training settings, and evaluation procedures in Section 5.1 and Appendix B are unchanged, including 90K training steps, batch size 16, Top-1 accuracy at IoU 0.95, and mIoU.

E4.justification: Both retain the component, attribute, and fusion ablations; expert-activation analyses by class and event strength; scene-complexity analyses; and qualitative failure cases. Material moving around appendix figures does not introduce additional analyses.

E5.justification: Both versions report point estimates without repeated-run or seed counts, error bars, confidence intervals, or statistical significance tests. No uncertainty-reporting practice is introduced or revised.

E6.justification: Numerical entries in Tables 2–5 and 14–16 are identical. For example, fusion EventRefer remains at 61.82% mAcc and 87.32% mIoU in Table 2. Dataset statistics, activation trends, and qualitative findings also match.

T1.justification: The task and voxel definitions, gating and matching equations, inference scoring, and event-response-strength definition and binning remain unchanged in Equations 1–9. No assumptions, derivations, or proofs are added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same claims concerning the first large-scale event-grounding benchmark, four-attribute annotations, and EventRefer's gains across the three modality settings.

C2.justification: Interpretations of attribute fusion and modality behavior are retained. Appendix C.3 preserves the same failure analysis, while Appendix D.3 retains the geographic, sensor, annotation-bias, grounding-scope, and synchronized-frame limitations.

D1.justification: v2 adds a direct talk2event/toolkit repository link under 'Code & Dataset' and separately labels the project homepage; v1 linked only to the homepage. Implementation details, hardware, prompts, and licenses remain unchanged.

R1.justification: Section 2's discussion of prior event-perception and grounding research is unchanged, as are all 118 references. The work's novelty positioning and relationship to earlier methods are retained.

P1.justification: v2 makes small wording and spacing edits, adds a NeurIPS 2025 footer, and moves acknowledgments from after the conclusion to before the references, adding thanks to reviewers and chairs. The scientific narrative is otherwise unchanged.

P2.justification: All 17 figures and 16 tables are retained without changed plots or table structures. Figure 2's caption adds the surrounding-frame timestamps, and Tables 12–13 receive small caption edits. Front-matter and acknowledgment changes cause limited layout reflow.

improvement.justification: The direct repository link improves documented resource access, and Figure 2's caption more explicitly identifies the surrounding frame times. These are limited usability gains; the methods, empirical evidence, statistical reporting, and limitations remain unchanged.
